findings.title: direct address opens without calling particle
findings.claim: The bare `rabbana` opens a direct appeal without an overt calling particle.
findings.mechanism: The noun of address itself carries the vocative force; its immediate arrival after the narrated Lord-relation changes third-person scene description into address.
findings.reader_payoff: The plea begins inside the exposed scene rather than after a separate speech-introduction formula.
findings.containment: This identifies the local address form only; it does not infer an unspoken particle or add a doctrine of rejection.

epistemic.reason: The local wording and aligned morphology directly support the bounded claim.

findings.title: our Lord makes the plea relational
findings.claim: The move from `their Lord` to `our Lord` makes the plea relational and personally directed.
findings.mechanism: The possessive suffix first locates the group before its Lord; the same title is then recast with first-person plural possession in direct address, turning exposure into appeal.
findings.reader_payoff: The speakers do not address an abstract authority: the relation they had just named becomes the relation to which they plead.
findings.containment: Retain the local possessive-to-vocative shift only. Do not claim that the address itself encodes prior denial, resistance, or an explicit confession of defiance.

epistemic.reason: The local wording and aligned morphology directly support the bounded claim.

findings.title: Lord echo shifts narration into speech
findings.claim: The echo from `rabbihim` to `rabbana` converts narrated Lordship into a direct plea.
findings.mechanism: The same noun first appears in third-person narration under `ʿinda`, then returns with first-person plural suffix as the speakers address the one before whom they stand.
findings.reader_payoff: A single repeated title bridges tableau and speech; the address feels forced out of the judgment scene itself.
findings.containment: This is a local discourse transition, not evidence that the two grammatical constructions have identical syntax or that the address succeeds.

epistemic.reason: The local wording and aligned morphology directly support the bounded claim.

findings.title: sight opens a total perception pair
findings.claim: Seeing and hearing form a compact two-faculty confession rather than an isolated report of sight.
findings.mechanism: The coordinated first-person perfects place visual and auditory recognition side by side, and the following request makes the pair the stated basis for action.
findings.reader_payoff: The plea admits that perception is now complete across more than one channel.
findings.containment: Keep the reading to the focus's coordinated sight/hearing pair; do not claim a surah-level repetition or import 32:9.

findings.title: first-person chain and hard onset intensify confession

findings.mechanism: The suffix `-nā` recurs through the clauses, while the hard onset in the perception sequence gives the confession a clipped, emphatic delivery before the request continues it.
findings.reader_payoff: The speakers cannot grammatically hand responsibility to someone else: the group that recognized the truth is the group promising to act.
findings.containment: This is a local pronoun-and-sound observation, not a claim that sound alone proves emotion or that every repeated ending has identical discourse force.

epistemic.reason: The local evidence supports the reading with the stated phonetic, contextual, or interpretive qualification.

findings.title: perfect verb claims sight has arrived

findings.reader_payoff: The line's tension is temporal: perception is stated as done, but righteous action remains conditional.
findings.containment: The perfect marks the asserted event as completed; it does not by itself specify when the seeing began or prove that every implication of the later plea is true.

epistemic.reason: The local wording and aligned morphology directly support the bounded claim.

findings.title: command form functions as plea

findings.title: request governs promised action

findings.containment: The fused form marks emphatic assertion, not the truth of the assertion or the speakers' sincerity.

findings.title: inna intensifies the closing claim

findings.reader_payoff: The appeal closes by pressing a claim of settled conviction precisely after asking for time to act on it.
findings.containment: Emphasis marks how the assertion is presented, not whether its content is genuine or sufficient.

epistemic.reason: The local wording and aligned morphology directly support the bounded claim.

findings.title: sound binds final assertion
